title: Longitudinal Associations Between Serum Superoxide Radical-Scavenging Capacity and Circulating α-Klotho in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis
content: Background/Objectives: We examined whether 3-month changes in MULTIS-derived serum superoxide radical-scavenging capacity were associated with changes in circulating α-Klotho during an intradialytic exercise program. Methods: This single-arm prospective observational study included 33 maintenance hemodialysis patients. Biomarkers were measured at baseline and 3 months, and change-score associations were assessed. Results: Mean α-Klotho decreased from 534 ± 177 to 448 ± 160 pg/mL (p = 0.004), and superoxide radical-scavenging capacity decreased from 0.53 ± 0.15 to 0.45 ± 0.12 U/mL SOD equivalents (p = 0.014). Despite these average decreases, changes were positively correlated (Pearson r = 0.406, p = 0.019; Spearman ρ = 0.446, p = 0.009). The age-, sex-, and dialysis vintage-adjusted coefficient was significant (p = 0.020), although the overall model was not (p = 0.189). The association was not significant after baseline adjustment (p = 0.095). Conclusions: This exploratory association was sensitive to baseline adjustment and does not establish a causal relationship or an exercise effect.
